doc.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Chapter One and Chapter Two sessions
summary: Both albums were done in two sessions of five or six hours, using friends who had not necessarily played together.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: How long did you have to do these records? Did they give you a day or two?

Yeah. Two sessions. That was called “Chapter One,” we did that in two, I guess five hour sessions, maybe six hours on one of them; and then the second one is called “Chapter Two” — surprise, surprise — the plot thickens. And that was about the same, I think maybe two six hour sessions, two afternoons.
Yeah, I was very thrilled with the results of those because it’s always kind of a calculated risk when you’re — well what I did is I took a lot of friends and favorite musicians of

mine who didn’t necessarily all know each other or even have played together, and I just could hear in my head that these guys would sound good together, and it worked in both cases. It doesn’t always work you know. You might have an all-star band and they don’t always click. But in these cases, I felt good about it.
